newsitem.title: USA: "Con Air" flies sky-high at U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Con Air" flies sky-high at U.S. box office.

text.p: The Nicolas Cage action movie "Con Air" overcame critical turbulence to fly to the top of the weekend U.S. box office, according to studio estimates released on Sunday.
The picture, in which Cage plays a paroled prisoner aboard a plane commandeered by a bunch of psychotic crooks, earned about $25.5 million for the Friday to Sunday period.

The No. 1 movie for the previous two weekends, "The Lost World: Jurassic Park," slipped to second with $18.5 million. Also down a notch, to third, was the romantic comedy, "Addicted to Love" with about $3.8 million.

The figures were provided by Exhibitor Relations Co., which collects the estimates from the studios. For the second week in a row, and just the fourth time this year, the overall box office was lower than the year-ago period. Final figures will be released on Monday.

If the "Con Air" estimates hold, the movie will have beaten the opening gross for Cage's "The Rock," which opened last July to $25.07 million. Both movies were produced by Jerry Bruckheimer and released by Walt Disney Co..

"The amazing thing for me is just how Jerry Bruckheimer seems to find a certain concept that the public is looking for every year," said Chuck Viane, senior vice-president of Disney's Buena Vista Pictures distribution unit.
Bruckheimer, together with his late partner Don Simpson, produced such movies as the first two "Beverly Hills Cop" movies, "Top Gun" and "Dangerous Minds." Simpson died of a drug overdose last year.
However, critics were not captivated by "Con Air." A Variety poll of reviewers in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago and Washington DC showed that 13 liked it, 20 did not, and 13 were mixed.
The movie averaged a sturdy $9,030 average from 2,824 screens, the highest average in the top 10. "Con Air" also opened this weekend in Britain, Hong Kong, Israel and several Latino markets.

The three-day total for "The Lost World: Jurassic Park" was 46 percent lower than last weekend's tally, and its per-screen average was $5,446. Its 18-day gross stands at $171 million. By comparison, 10th-place "Liar Liar" has earned $168.5 million after 80 days of release.
"Addicted to Love" averaged just $1,880 per screen, as its 17-day total rose to $26.4 million.

The only other new entry in the top 10 was "Buddy," starring Rene Russo raising a chimp as a member of her household. It opened in fourth with $3.7 million, a meagre $1,751 average and underwhelming reviews. According to Variety, seven critics liked it, 10 did not and 20 were mixed.
"Gone Fishin'," a comedy that debuted last weekend, slipped two places to fifth with $3.1 million, and a $1,679 average. Its gross to date stands at $10.6 million.
"Con Air" and "Gone Fishin'" are released by Walt Disney Co..
"The Lost World: Jurassic Park" and "Liar Liar" are released by Universal Pictures, a unit of Seagram Co. Ltd. .
"Addicted To Love" is released by Warner Bros, a unit of Time Warner Inc..
"Buddy" is released by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp..
